title: Masoor Daal (Red Lentils)

source.text: S. Abbas Raza, Pakistani & North Indian Cooking (2015)

description: The quickest and most common daal: salmon-colored lentils that cook to yellow, finished with a smoky garlic and chili tarka. Goes with almost anything.

steps.action: Rinse in a small pot until the water runs almost clear (removes starch that makes grains stick); drain well:
Add and heat on high; stir once as it starts to boil, then skim off the white foam:
Reduce to medium-low (3/10) to a simmer; stir in:
Cover; cook 20 min, stirring and scraping every 5 min.
Check: porridge-like (add water if too thick) and grains mash easily against the pot. If not, cook 5 min more and repeat. Turn off heat; keep covered.
Tarka: heat in a small frying pan over high, 2 min:
Add and fry, stirring, until the garlic is light brown; move fast, it burns quickly after:
items: 6 medium garlic cloves, thinly sliced (about 2 mm / ¹⁄₁₆ in)

steps.action: Stir the daal once; pour in the tarka slowly (it splatters), scraping the pan. Stir until mixed. Adjust salt.

items: Almost any meat, fish, vegetable, rice, or bread
The chilies are hot; eat them or set aside
